body: Using Node.js ensures cross-platform consistency and readability. Writing file matching, stats checking, and custom error reporting logic in Shell/bash scripts can become verbose and error-prone due to platform differences (e.g. BSD vs GNU commands), whereas a pure Node.js JS script runs consistently across all machines.

Yes, `this.name = ...` is mandatory when subclassing `Error`. In JS/TS, standard instances inherit `name = 'Error'` from the prototype. Without explicitly setting `this.name = 'ScraperHttpError'` in the constructor, `error.name` would incorrectly print as `'Error'`, breaking name-based formatting in ErrorCard and tests.

Yes, we need `ScraperUnknownError`. When unexpected subscription errors or general runtime exceptions (like standard Javascript TypeErrors) occur in the scanning pipeline, they are caught and wrapped in `ScraperUnknownError` to ensure they implement the ScraperError interface uniformly, preventing the UI/ErrorCard from throwing undefined property errors.
Done. We've made `url` a mandatory property in the `ScraperError` base constructor.

Done. We have renamed `ScraperParseStep` to `ScraperScanStep`, elevated `scanStep` to the `ScraperError` base class, and made it mandatory for all errors (with `ScraperUnknownError` defaulting to `SYSTEM` and `ScraperHttpError` defaulting to `PAGINATION`).
Done. Updated the docstring to specify non-2xx/3xx HTTP response status codes (e.g. 404, 500, 502).
